source: hand-authored from mockserver-core 8.0.0 JsonSchemaValidatorRemoteRefTest: the JUnit test calls JsonSchemaValidator in-process with no wire form of its own, so these steps translate its 5 cases into the JSON_SCHEMA body matcher on the data plane, which shares the same validator. shouldExposeRemoteRefsBlockedByDefault and the flag-only half of shouldAllowRemoteRefsWhenSystemPropertyOptIn assert a static getter directly and have no wire form either; both are ported as Rust unit tests instead (src/matcher/string.rs, src/matcher/body.rs).

steps.note: register: an internal-$ref schema (unaffected by the SSRF gate) and a remote-$ref schema (RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1, guaranteed non-routable — the point is that it is never actually contacted)
shouldMatchSchemaUsingOnlyInternalRefsAsBefore: a schema with only internal ($ref: #/...) refs validates exactly as before the SSRF gate

shouldRejectNonMatchingBodyAgainstInternalRefSchemaAsBefore: a body violating the internal ref's minimum:1 is reported as a non-match, mentioning "count" — the gate changes nothing about internal-ref validation

shouldBlockRemoteRefByDefaultWithoutNetworkFetch: the remote $ref is never fetched (default deny, no opt-in) — the response comes back promptly (this step would hang/timeout if the server actually tried to reach 192.0.2.1) and the closest-match hint names the blocked reference instead of a connection failure
